_source: AIE #94 6175255841 (14 Oct, AMEND of #3097): the exact CAPACITY CHAIN. paragraph, applied once in place of PROMPT's STATED CAPACITY CHAIN text
chain: CAPACITY CHAIN. When the brief supplies the parts of the team’s allocation to the same deliverable, retain their actual quantities, units, population, period, source and qualifications. Declare a product identity only where that arithmetic is valid: headcount multiplied by the share of time on this work gives allocated developer-equivalents, with a percentage converted to a fraction once. Keep the supplied inputs distinct from derived values and Olumi’s interpretation; do not present the identity or its effect on delivery speed as a human assertion unless it was supplied as such. A stated share on legacy fixes does not by itself establish that all remaining time is feature work. Derive complementary shares only for an explicitly complete, disjoint allocation of the same whole; otherwise any proposed allocation is labelled as Olumi’s assumption, with its basis and unresolved conditions. An option changing that allocation sets its affected parts consistently with the retained whole, without inventing other categories or changing stated bounds. A setting the brief does not give remains ai_proposed, with no fabricated stated evidence. A time-freeing option represented by this allocation chain has added_capacity null, so the same effect is not counted again as a separate pace contribution. Preserve the chain’s original factors and causal meaning; downstream computation must also apply each effect once. Arithmetic allocation is not evidence that delivery pace scales proportionally, that the change is immediately effective, or that skill, onboarding, transition costs and other risks are absent. Retain those separate causal, timing and uncertainty assumptions and all governing conditions as provisional reasoning for the existing analysis and proposal paths.
